record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties
record.context_brief: Commutative nonexpansive semigroup actions on c0
record.original_question: Let C be a nonempty closed convex subset of the sequence space c_0, and let S be a commutative semigroup acting on C by nonexpansive mappings {T_s : s in S}. If for some c in C the orbit {T_s c : s in S} is relatively weakly compact, must C contain a common fixed point for S?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.13. Let C be a nonempty closed convex subset of the sequence space c0 and S = {Tsc : s ∈ S} be a representation of a commutative semigroup S as nonexpansive mappings on C. Suppose that {Tsc : s ∈ S} is relatively weakly compact for some c ∈ C. Does C contain a common fixed point for S?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real sequences converging to $0$, equipped with the supremum norm. Let $C$ be a nonempty closed convex subset of $c_0$, and let $S$ be a commutative semigroup. Suppose $\{T_s : s \in S\}$ is a representation of $S$ as nonexpansive self-mappings of $C$; that is, each $T_s : C \to C$ satisfies $\|T_s x - T_s y\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in C$, and $T_{st} = T_s \circ T_t$ for all $s, t \in S$. Assume there exists some $c \in C$ such that the orbit $\{T_s c : s \in S\}$ is relatively weakly compact in $c_0$. Must there exist a point $x \in C$ with $T_s x = x$ for every $s \in S$?
artifact.category_tag: Fixed point theory for nonexpansive semigroups
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related results on fixed points of commuting nonexpansive mappings, weakly compact sets in c_0, and the fixed point property characterization of weak compactness in c_0, but no source claims a resolution to this specific question about common fixed points for commutative nonexpansive semigroups on c_0 with a relatively weakly compact orbit. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Characterizations of weakly compact sets and new fixed point free maps in c_0
status_evidence.snippet: For closed, bounded, convex subsets C of c_0, weak compactness can be characterized: such a C is weakly compact iff all of its closed, convex, nonempty subsets have the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings.
status_evidence.claim: Related background on the relationship between weak compactness in c_0 and the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings; does not resolve the semigroup version.

status_evidence.title: Normal Structure and Common Fixed Point Properties for Semigroups of Nonexpansive Mappings in Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Common fixed point results require structural hypotheses (normal structure, weak compactness of C) beyond mere relatively weakly compact orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Existing common fixed point theorems in this area do not cover the c_0 setting with only a relatively weakly compact orbit, suggesting the problem remains open.
